title: one day of Ramadan
hookLine: a kitchen at four in the morning: one day of the fast, from suhoor to iftar

lines: A KITCHEN AT FOUR IN THE MORNING.
cards: Four in the morning, and the kitchen light is on. A family, half asleep, eating dates and eggs and drinking as much water as they can before the sky starts to pale.
Then, from dawn, nothing: no food, not even a sip of water, until sunset. If you grew up with it, you know every hour of that day. It's rarely told start to finish, with what it's for.

teach.b: Ramadan is a month of the Islamic calendar, which follows the moon, so it slides earlier every year and passes through every season. Here's one day of it. Before dawn, suhoor, the early meal.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said there's a blessing in it, so people eat even when they'd rather sleep.

teach.h: DAWN TO SUNSET: NO FOOD, NO WATER.
teach.b: At first light comes the dawn prayer, and the fast begins: no food, no drink, until sunset. That's the fourth pillar, sawm. Then the day itself: work, school, errands, and a hunger that keeps tapping you on the shoulder.

teach.h: THAT YE MAY WARD OFF EVIL.
teach.b: The Qur'an says it plainly: “Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil).” The word underneath is taqwa, a careful awareness.
The hunger is a tool, not the point. Another of the Prophet's sayings makes that sharp: whoever doesn't give up lying, God has no need of their giving up food and drink.

At sunset, iftar: the fast breaks, often with a date and water, the way the Prophet broke his. And it's built for real people: the sick and travelers are excused, and make the days up later. Why this month?
The Qur'an names it as the month the Qur'an was revealed.

how: During Ramadan, adult Muslims who are able fast from dawn to sunset, eat a pre-dawn meal called suhoor, break the fast at sunset with iftar, often with dates and water, and many mosques hold extra night prayers.

games.q: one day of the fast — tap the pairs.
p: careful awareness: what the fast is for

s: Ramadan falls at the same time every year
it follows the moon, so it moves earlier each year, through every season.
water is allowed during the fast
no food and no drink, not even water, from dawn to sunset.
the sick and travelers may make up missed days later

games.q: it's Ramadan. you've fasted all day, and at four in the afternoon a coworker says something that makes you furious. what does the Prophet's ﷺ saying suggest about your fast?
o: as long as you haven't eaten, it's fine.
a sharp tongue can empty the fast of its point.
anger breaks the fast, so you may as well eat.
games.why: the hunger is a tool, not the point. God has no need of the fast of someone who won't give up lying.

games.q: put one day of Ramadan in order.
p: the dawn prayer: the fast begins
the long day, no food or water
iftar at sunset, often a date

practice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, notice your body: is there any hunger or thirst in it, even a little? On the second, picture the next thing you'll eat or drink.
On the third, picture that first sip, taken slowly, the way it's taken at sunset.

wordCard.voice: Ramadan. The month of the fast, dawn to sunset, and the month the Qur'an was revealed. Sixth word.

orig.note: Arabic: the month of the fast, often linked to r-m-d, a root for scorching heat.

carryVoice: Your line: hunger teaches. The empty hours are where the attention grows. See you tomorrow.
